title: Job, Chapter 9 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Job 9 on folio 399v of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Job chapter 9 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folio 399v.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ <sup>2</sup>אָ֭מְנָם יָדַ֣עְתִּי כִי־כֵ֑ן וּמַה־יִּצְדַּ֖ק אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עִם־אֵֽל׃ <sup>3</sup>אִם־יַ֭חְפֹּץ לָרִ֣יב עִמּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־יַ֝עֲנֶ֗נּוּ אַחַ֥ת מִנִּי־אָֽלֶף׃ <sup>4</sup>חֲכַ֣ם לֵ֭בָב וְאַמִּ֣יץ כֹּ֑חַ מִֽי־הִקְשָׁ֥ה אֵ֝לָ֗יו וַיִּשְׁלָֽם׃ <sup>5</sup>הַמַּעְתִּ֣יק הָ֭רִים וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑עוּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר הֲפָכָ֣ם בְּאַפּֽוֹ׃ <sup>6</sup>הַמַּרְגִּ֣יז אֶ֭רֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָ֑הּ וְ֝עַמּוּדֶ֗יהָ יִתְפַלָּצֽוּן׃ <sup>7</sup>הָאֹמֵ֣ר לַ֭חֶרֶס וְלֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ח וּבְעַ֖ד כּוֹכָבִ֣ים יַחְתֹּֽם׃ <sup>8</sup>נֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַ֣יִם לְבַדּ֑וֹ וְ֝דוֹרֵ֗ךְ עַל־בָּ֥מֳתֵי יָֽם׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Then Job answered and said, <sup>2</sup>I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God? <sup>3</sup>If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand. <sup>4</sup>He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered? <sup>5</sup>Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger. <sup>6</sup>Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble. <sup>7</sup>Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars. <sup>8</sup>Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>עֹֽשֶׂה־עָ֭שׁ כְּסִ֥יל וְכִימָ֗ה וְחַדְרֵ֥י תֵמָֽן׃ <sup>10</sup>עֹשֶׂ֣ה גְ֭דֹלוֹת עַד־אֵ֣ין חֵ֑קֶר וְ֝נִפְלָא֗וֹת עַד־אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃ <sup>11</sup>הֵ֤ן יַעֲבֹ֣ר עָ֭לַי וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶ֑ה וְ֝יַחֲלֹ֗ף וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃ <sup>12</sup>הֵ֣ן יַ֭חְתֹּף מִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ מִֽי־יֹאמַ֥ר אֵ֝לָ֗יו מַֽה־תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃ <sup>13</sup>אֱ֭לוֹהַּ לֹא־יָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ תחתו [תַּחְתָּ֥יו] שָׁ֝חֲח֗וּ עֹ֣זְרֵי רָֽהַב׃ <sup>14</sup>אַ֭ף כִּֽי־אָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ אֶבְחֲרָ֖ה דְבָרַ֣י עִמּוֹ׃ <sup>15</sup>אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם־צָ֭דַקְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶעֱנֶ֑ה לִ֝מְשֹׁפְטִ֗י אֶתְחַנָּֽן׃ <sup>16</sup>אִם־קָרָ֥אתִי וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑נִי לֹֽא־אַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּֽי־יַאֲזִ֥ין קוֹלִֽי׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south. <sup>10</sup>Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number. <sup>11</sup>Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not. <sup>12</sup>Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou? <sup>13</sup>If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him. <sup>14</sup>How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him? <sup>15</sup>Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge. <sup>16</sup>If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>אֲשֶׁר־בִּשְׂעָרָ֥ה יְשׁוּפֵ֑נִי וְהִרְבָּ֖ה פְצָעַ֣י חִנָּֽם׃ <sup>18</sup>לֹֽא־יִ֭תְּנֵנִי הָשֵׁ֣ב רוּחִ֑י כִּ֥י יַ֝שְׂבִּעַ֗נִי מַמְּרֹרִֽים׃ <sup>19</sup>אִם־לְכֹ֣חַ אַמִּ֣יץ הִנֵּ֑ה וְאִם־לְ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט מִ֣י יוֹעִידֵֽנִי׃ <sup>20</sup>אִם־אֶ֭צְדָּק פִּ֣י יַרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי תָּֽם־אָ֝֗נִי וַֽיַּעְקְשֵֽׁנִי׃ <sup>21</sup>תָּֽם־אָ֭נִי לֹֽא־אֵדַ֥ע נַפְשִׁ֗י אֶמְאַ֥ס חַיָּֽי׃ <sup>22</sup>אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל־כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֑רְתִּי תָּ֥ם וְ֝רָשָׁ֗ע ה֣וּא מְכַלֶּֽה׃ <sup>23</sup>אִם־שׁ֭וֹט יָמִ֣ית פִּתְאֹ֑ם לְמַסַּ֖ת נְקִיִּ֣ם יִלְעָֽג׃ <sup>24</sup>אֶ֤רֶץ ׀ נִתְּנָ֬ה בְֽיַד־רָשָׁ֗ע פְּנֵֽי־שֹׁפְטֶ֥יהָ יְכַסֶּ֑ה אִם־לֹ֖א אֵפ֣וֹא מִי־הֽוּא׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause. <sup>18</sup>He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness. <sup>19</sup>If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead? <sup>20</sup>If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse. <sup>21</sup>Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life. <sup>22</sup>This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked. <sup>23</sup>If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent. <sup>24</sup>The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>וְיָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי־רָ֑ץ בָּֽ֝רְח֗וּ לֹא־רָא֥וּ טוֹבָֽה׃ <sup>26</sup>חָ֭לְפוּ עִם־אֳנִיּ֣וֹת אֵבֶ֑ה כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר יָט֥וּשׂ עֲלֵי־אֹֽכֶל׃ <sup>27</sup>אִם־אָ֭מְרִי אֶשְׁכְּחָ֣ה שִׂיחִ֑י אֶעֶזְבָ֖ה פָנַ֣י וְאַבְלִֽיגָה׃ <sup>28</sup>יָגֹ֥רְתִּי כָל־עַצְּבֹתָ֑י יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּי־לֹ֥א תְנַקֵּֽנִי׃ <sup>29</sup>אָנֹכִ֥י אֶרְשָׁ֑ע לָמָּה־זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל אִיגָֽע׃ <sup>30</sup>אִם־הִתְרָחַ֥צְתִּי במו־ [בְמֵי־] שָׁ֑לֶג וַ֝הֲזִכּ֗וֹתִי בְּבֹ֣ר כַּפָּי׃ <sup>31</sup>אָ֭ז בַּשַּׁ֣חַת תִּטְבְּלֵ֑נִי וְ֝תִֽעֲב֗וּנִי שַׂלְמוֹתָֽי׃ <sup>32</sup>כִּי־לֹא־אִ֣ישׁ כָּמֹ֣נִי אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ נָב֥וֹא יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good. <sup>26</sup>They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey. <sup>27</sup>If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself: <sup>28</sup>I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent. <sup>29</sup>If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain? <sup>30</sup>If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean; <sup>31</sup>Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me. <sup>32</sup>For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.

translation.original_text: <sup>33</sup>לֹ֣א יֵשׁ־בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ מוֹכִ֑יחַ יָשֵׁ֖ת יָד֣וֹ עַל־שְׁנֵֽינוּ׃ <sup>34</sup>יָסֵ֣ר מֵעָלַ֣י שִׁבְט֑וֹ וְ֝אֵמָת֗וֹ אַֽל־תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃ <sup>35</sup>אַֽ֭דַבְּרָה וְלֹ֣א אִירָאֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־כֵ֥ן אָ֝נֹכִ֗י עִמָּדִֽי׃
translation.text: <sup>33</sup>Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both. <sup>34</sup>Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me: <sup>35</sup>Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.
